title: An evolution game I have tried to make over and over for decades that finally came together with ai
author: baronvonpain
selftext:
I have been coding since well into the 90s, and have been doing so in a professional sense for about 23 years, with the last 12 or so being my main line of work. I'm very good, and very very fast, but I'm also full of crazy ideas and some of them were too complicated to get working the way I wanted without intense focus. And since no one refers to me as Mr. Focus, this is one of those. I first tried building this game in Flash in the early 2000s and it didn't work at all. I then made a version of the animal portion on the iPad, and had a few other iterations after, but the full breadth of it never functioned like it should.

Anyway, here's what the game is about:

In this game you play with other players in one world. You are given the option to play as a plant, animal, or microbe.   
  
The plants can only see other plants, and are focused on spreading around and growing fruit that will affect the animals. They are able to control the breeze of their pollination, that it's possible that someone's plants will crossbreed with someone else's plants.

The animals can see other animals and plants, and can adapt based on points they get from living their lives. These adaptations are then passed on to offspring that are created when two players "mate". They lay an egg that can then be possessed by another random player coming in, or if you make a nest you can invite up to three friends. Starting a new species gives you a small blob of a creature, and from there you can adapt with better vision, legs, wings, tails, spikes, and all kinds of other things that can then be passed onto offspring. Whether they survive with these traits is determined by the environment that has been created in the world.

Microbes can only see themselves and references to animals. The options for microbes are viruses, bacteria, and fungi. They float around and only have a certain amount of time outside a host before they will die (unless they are a fungi and attach themselves to the ground). Their adaptations allow them to change attributes on animals that are infected, making them different colors, bumpy, slow, smelly, and more. 

I'm still developing this so there may be issues. Let me know if there are and I'll try to fix them. I'm using Claude to put this one together and it's compressed the amount of time I need to spend on it to next to nothing relatively speaking, so hopefully I'll be able to wrap it up very soon. I am a million project nonsense kind of guy, but if people are interested in this I'll dedicate more time to it. Right now, it's just one of my fun late night hobby projects, and I have a lot of them.

comments.author: Short_Stable2397
comments.body:
It's just a feeling from reading your post, nothing concrete, but you probably want to have them all 'co-existing' more. Maybe just coming up with more cross class interactions because at the moment plants are only support roles and there would be less incentive to play them as a result.

Best of luck with your game, now is definitely the right time to pick it up again!
